user.title: Cerberus WAN
user.description:
Detected right now: {detected}.

The network you are going out through is already in the table below, without a name. Open the link to see who it belongs to, then type the name you want the sensor to show:

`35612 = Eolo;`

Every provider is closed by a semicolon. It is needed: two providers that end up on the same line without one are read as a single provider, and the number of the second lands inside the name of the first. You do not have to add them all now: whenever the sensor shows the unknown label, reopen this dialog and the network in use, along with the ones you have been going out through lately, will be waiting here for a name. You do not have to do it while the failover is happening.

Optionally pick an automation or a script to start whenever the provider changes. You can also leave this empty and trigger on the `cerberus_wan_provider_changed` event, which carries what changed.

init.title: Cerberus WAN
init.description:
Detected right now: {detected}.

The networks still without a name are at the bottom of the table: the one in use first, then the ones you have gone out through in the last few weeks. The backup line can be named at leisure, long after the failover ended. Open the link to see who it belongs to, then type the name you want the sensor to show:

`35612 = Eolo;`

Every provider is closed by a semicolon, so you can write after the last row without joining it to the one before. Rows that cannot be read are ignored, so a typo costs one provider and never a dialog that refuses to close.

Automations and scripts to start whenever the provider changes. Automations keep their own conditions; scripts receive the old and new provider as variables. Leaving this empty changes nothing else: the `cerberus_wan_provider_changed` event is fired either way.
